exercise_group.instruction: Exercises 1–4 display sets in $$\mathbf{\mathbb{R}}^{2}$$ ﻿. Assume the sets include the bounding lines. In each case, give a specific reason why the set $$H$$ is not a subspace of $$\mathbf{\mathbb{R}}^{2}$$ ﻿. (For instance, find two vectors in $$H$$ whose sum is not in $$H$$ ﻿, or find a vector in $$H$$ with a scalar multiple that is not in $$H$$ ﻿. Draw a picture.)

problem.paragraph: Let $$\textbf{v}_{1} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 3 \\ - 5 \end{bmatrix} ,$$ $$\textbf{v}_{2} = \left\lbrack \begin{array}{r} {- 4} \\ {- 5} \\ 8 \end{array} \right\rbrack,$$ and $$\textbf{w} = \left\lbrack \begin{array}{r} 8 \\ 2 \\ {- 9} \end{array} \right\rbrack$$ . Determine if $$\mathbf{w}$$ is in the subspace of $$\mathbf{\mathbb{R}}^{3}$$ generated by $$\textbf{v}_{1}$$ and $$\textbf{v}_{2}$$ .﻿

Let $$\textbf{v}_{1} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ - 2 \\ 4 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix} ,$$ $$\textbf{v}_{2} = \begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ - 7 \\ 9 \\ 7 \end{bmatrix} ,$$ $$\textbf{v}_{3} = \left\lbrack \begin{array}{r} 5 \\ {- 8} \\ 6 \\ 5 \end{array} \right\rbrack,$$ and $$\textbf{u} = \left\lbrack \begin{array}{r} {- 4} \\ 10 \\ {- 7} \\ {- 5} \end{array} \right\rbrack$$ . Determine if $$\mathbf{u}$$ is in the subspace of $$\mathbf{\mathbb{R}}^{4}$$ generated by $$\{\textbf{v}_{1},\textbf{v}_{2},\textbf{v}_{3}\}$$ .﻿

Let $$\textbf{v}_{1} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ - 8 \\ 6 \end{bmatrix} ,$$ $$\textbf{v}_{2} = \begin{bmatrix} - 3 \\ 8 \\ - 7 \end{bmatrix} ,$$ $$\textbf{v}_{3} = \begin{bmatrix} - 4 \\ 6 \\ - 7 \end{bmatrix} ,$$ $$\textbf{p} = \left\lbrack \begin{array}{r} 6 \\ {- 10} \\ 11 \end{array} \right\rbrack,$$ and $$A = \left[\right. \mathbf{v}_{1} \mathbf{v}_{2} \mathbf{v}_{3} \left]\right. .$$

list.item: How many vectors are in Col $$A$$ ?

exercise_group.instruction: In Exercises 21–30, mark each statement Ture or False (T/F). Justify each answer.

problem.paragraph: (T/F) A subspace of $$\mathbf{\mathbb{R}}^{n}$$ is any set $$H$$ such that (i) the zero vector is in $$H$$ , (ii) $$\textbf{u}$$ , $$\textbf{v}$$ , and $$\textbf{u} + \textbf{v}$$ are in $$H$$ , and (iii) $$c$$ is a scalar and $$c\textbf{u}$$ is in $$H$$ .﻿
(T/F) A subset $$H$$ of $$\mathbf{\mathbb{R}}^{n}$$ is a subspace if the zero vector is in $$H$$ .﻿

(T/F) If $$\textbf{v}_{1},\ldots,\textbf{v}_{p}$$ are in $$\mathbf{\mathbb{R}}^{n}$$ , then Span $$\{\textbf{v}_{1},\ldots,\textbf{v}_{p}\}$$ is the same as the column space of the matrix $$\lbrack\textbf{v}_{1}\ldots\textbf{v}_{p}\rbrack$$ .﻿
(T/F) Given vectors $$\textbf{v}_{1},\ldots,\textbf{v}_{p}$$ in $$\mathbf{\mathbb{R}}^{n}$$ , the set of all linear combinations of these vectors is a subspace of $$\mathbf{\mathbb{R}}^{n}$$ .﻿
(T/F) The set of all solutions of a system of $$m$$ homogeneous equations in $$n$$ unknowns is a subspace of $$\mathbf{\mathbb{R}}^{m}$$ .﻿
(T/F) The null space of an $$m \times n$$ matrix is a subspace of $$\mathbf{\mathbb{R}}^{n}$$ .﻿
(T/F) The columns of an invertible $$n \times n$$ matrix form a basis for $$\mathbf{\mathbb{R}}^{n}$$ .﻿
(T/F) The column space of a matrix $$A$$ is the set of solutions of $$A\textbf{x} = \textbf{b}$$ .﻿
(T/F) Row operations do not affect linear dependence relations among the columns of a matrix.
(T/F) If $$B$$ is an echelon form of a matrix $$A,$$ then the pivot columns of $$B$$ form a basis for Col $$A$$ .﻿

Suppose the columns of a matrix $$A = \lbrack\textbf{a}_{1} \cdots \textbf{a}_{p}\rbrack$$ are linearly independent. Explain why $$\{\textbf{a}_{1},\ldots,\textbf{a}_{p}\}$$ is a basis for Col $$A$$ .﻿

exercise_group.instruction: In Exercises 45 and 46, construct bases for the column space and the null space of the given matrix $$A$$ Justify your work.

problem.paragraph: To determine whether $$\textbf{u}$$ is in $$\text{Nul} A,$$ simply compute $$A \textbf{u} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & - 1 & 5 \\ 2 & 0 & 7 \\ - 3 & - 5 & - 3 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} - 7 \\ 3 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}$$

The result shows that $$\textbf{u}$$ is in $$\text{Nul} A.$$ Deciding whether $$\textbf{u}$$ is in $$\text{Col} A$$ requires more work. Reduce the augmented matrix $$\lbrack A \textbf{u}\rbrack$$ to echelon form to determine whether the equation $$A\textbf{x} = \textbf{u}$$ is consistent: $$\begin{bmatrix} 1 & - 1 & 5 \\ 2 & 0 & 7 \\ - 3 & - 5 & - 3 - 7 \\ 3 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix} \sim \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \\ 0 - 1 \\ 2 \\ - 8 - 5 \\ - 3 \\ 12 - 7 \\ 17 \\ 19 \end{bmatrix} \sim \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \\ 0 - 1 \\ 2 \\ 0 5 \\ - 3 \\ 0 - 7 \\ 17 \\ 49 \end{bmatrix}$$
The equation $$A\textbf{x} = \textbf{u}$$ has no solution, so $$\textbf{u}$$ is not in $$\text{Col} A$$ .﻿

In contrast to Practice Problem 1, finding a vector in $$\text{Nul} A$$ requires more work than testing whether a specified vector is in $$\text{Nul} A$$ . However, since $$A$$ is already in reduced echelon form, the equation $$A\textbf{x} = \textbf{0}$$ shows that if $$\textbf{x} = \left( x_{1},x_{2},x_{3} \right)$$ , then $$x_{2} = 0$$ , $$x_{3} = 0$$ , and $$x_{1}$$ is a free variable. Thus, a basis for $$\text{Nul} A$$ is $$\textbf{v} = (1,0,0).$$ Finding just one vector in $$\text{Col} A$$ is trivial, since each column of $$A$$ is in $$\text{Col} A$$ . In this particular case, the same vector $$\textbf{v}$$ is in both $$\text{Nul} A$$ and $$\text{Col} A$$ . For most $$n \times n$$ matrices, the zero vector of $$\mathbf{\mathbb{R}}^{n}$$ is the only vector in both $$\text{Nul} A$$ and $$\text{Col} A$$ .﻿

If $$A$$ is invertible, then the columns of $$A$$ span $$\mathbf{\mathbb{R}}^{n}$$ , by the Invertible Matrix Theorem. By definition, the columns of any matrix always span the column space, so in this case $$\text{Col} A$$ is all of $$\mathbf{\mathbb{R}}^{n}.$$ In symbols, $$\text{Col} A = \mathbf{\mathbb{R}}^{n}.$$ Also, since $$A$$ is invertible, the equation $$A\textbf{x} = \textbf{0}$$ has only the trivial solution. This means that $$\text{Nul} A$$ is the zero subspace. In symbols, $$\text{Nul} A = \left{\right. \textbf{0} \left.\right} .$$
